narr: Training of heavy thunderstorms produced flash flooding across central Mississippi and the Interstate 20 corridor.
ev: A part of Decatur Stratton Road was flooded.
A portion of Pattison-Tillman Road flooded.
Several streets and roads were flooded in Pearl.
Two businesses in Monticello were flooded, and a few streets were flooded.
Parts of Quail Hill Road were flooded.
McRaven Street and Main street were flooded.
A part of US Highway 80 near Chunky was flooded, and a portion of Beason Road was partially washed out.
A few roads in central Scott County were flooded including portions of Old Jackson Road, MS Highway 21, and Sparksville Road.

Multiple roads were flooded in Jackson including Williams Drive, Hattiesburg Street near Jim Hill High School, Gallatin Street, and the Monument Street underpass at Town Creek where a vehicle stalled in floodwaters.
Part of County Road 23 was flooded.
A few roads in the southern half of Lawrence County were briefly flooded.
A few roads in the northern part of Lamar County were flooded.

A few roads in the southern part of Rankin County were flooded over including parts of Monterey Road, Star Road, and Williams Road. A car was submerged in floodwater near the intersection of Old Pearson Road and Peggy Road in Florence.
Part of MS Highway 513 was flooded.

Several roads in and near Meridian were flooded including Bolen Long Creek Road, 65th Avenue near Laurel Drive, King Rd, Newell Rd, US Highway 11, TM Jones Rd, Old Wire Rd, Bronson Rd, Cow Creek Rd, Arundel Rd, and State Blvd. Flooding along MS Highway 496 near Harper Road caused a portion of the road to wash out. There was also flooding at the Meridian Crossroads Shopping Center.
A creek near Byram flowed out of its banks.
A portion of MS Highway 468 was under water.
Parts of Gulde Road near US Highway 80 were flooded up to two feet deep.
A creek near Utica overflowed its banks.
Part of the intersection of Service Drive and Gateway Drive were flooded.
